evidence.claim: The federal executive authority is exercised through the Prime Minister, who is the chief executive of the Federation, and the Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly.
evidence.title: Chapter 3: The Federal Government
evidence.publisher: pakistani.org (text of the Constitution of Pakistan)
evidence.excerpt: The federal executive authority is exercised through the Prime Minister, who is the chief executive of the Federation, and the Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct constitutional text from the governing legal framework.
evidence.period_fit: Directly applicable to 2022 office authority and parliamentary dependence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Shehbaz Sharif's formal office and confidence dependence, but not personal control of nuclear policy.
contrary_evidence: Formal chief-executive status does not prove direct operational control over nuclear forces or security institutions.

evidence.claim: The Federal Government has control and command of the Armed Forces.
evidence.title: Chapter 2: Armed Forces
evidence.publisher: pakistani.org (text of the Constitution of Pakistan)
evidence.excerpt: The Federal Government has control and command of the Armed Forces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct constitutional text on state command authority.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows the formal state command structure under Sharif's government, but not a target-period nuclear decision by Sharif personally.
contrary_evidence: This general command clause does not by itself show day-to-day nuclear command or how much practical autonomy the military retained.

evidence.claim: Women, religious minorities, and transgender people continued to face violence, discrimination, and persecution, while authorities failed to provide adequate protection or hold perpetrators to account.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Women, religious minorities, and transgender people continued to face violence, discrimination, and persecution, while authorities failed to provide adequate protection or hold perpetrators to account.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Year-end human-rights synthesis with multiple specific examples across vulnerable groups.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This describes state protection failures under Sharif's government, but much of the violence was perpetrated by non-state actors or inherited institutions.
contrary_evidence: The report does not show a single Sharif-directed campaign against these groups; it shows a failure to protect and remedy.

evidence.claim: Pakistan's military exerts enormous influence, intimidates the media, and enjoys impunity for indiscriminate or extralegal use of force.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan's military exerts enormous influence, intimidates the media, and enjoys impunity for indiscriminate or extralegal use of force.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Established democracy/rights monitor with a concise country overview and year-end synthesis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is partly inherited structural context, but it also constrains and shapes what the Sharif government could or did do about security-force abuse and media pressure.
contrary_evidence: The statement is structural and not a direct account of a specific Sharif instruction or event.

evidence.claim: Police arrested journalists Jameel Farooqui and Ilyas Samoo, and CPJ said authorities should stop harassing them in retaliation for their work and release them immediately.
evidence.title: Pakistani journalists Jameel Farooqui and Ilyas Samoo arrested; Farooqui remains in detention
evidence.excerpt: Police arrested journalists Jameel Farooqui and Ilyas Samoo, and CPJ said authorities should stop harassing them in retaliation for their work and release them immediately.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous alert with named actors, arrest dates, and direct attribution to police action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sharif-led domestic environment, but the arrests were made by provincial police, not the PM personally.
contrary_evidence: The case file references public-order or criminal allegations, so the evidence is about retaliation risk and abuse of process rather than a final legal judgment.

evidence.claim: Peaceful protests by families of the disappeared were met with intimidation, harassment, arbitrary detention, and violence by state actors, including unnecessary force against protesters in Karachi.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Braving the Storm: Enforced disappearances and the right to protest in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Peaceful protests by families of the disappeared were met with intimidation, harassment, arbitrary detention, and violence by state actors, including unnecessary force against protesters in Karachi.
evidence.source_locator: briefing summary and the Karachi protest account
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed rights briefing with specific protest incidents and first-hand accounts.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period and directly about 2022 protest handling.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects state conduct under Sharif's government, but the abuse appears to have been carried out by police and intelligence agents rather than ordered in a public PM statement.
contrary_evidence: The protests concerned enforced disappearances inherited from prior years, so the state failure is partly long-running rather than newly created in 2022.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said authorities used unnecessary or excessive force to disperse Lyari protesters over power shortages, describing baton-charging and tear-gassing of people exercising their right to protest.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Authorities must respect and facilitate people’s right to protest
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said authorities used unnecessary or excessive force to disperse Lyari protesters over power shortages, describing baton-charging and tear-gassing of people exercising their right to protest.
evidence.source_locator: quoted response paragraphs and background section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights statement tied to a specific protest and police response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This was police conduct under the Sharif government, but not a PM-only action and not proof of a centrally ordered repression policy by itself.
contrary_evidence: Police said the protests blocked traffic, so the case involves a public-order dispute as well as a rights violation allegation.

evidence.claim: After Imran Khan was shot, his supporters staged nationwide protests that sometimes clashed with security forces, and police used tear gas to disperse protesters blocking roads.
evidence.title: Ex-Pakistani PM Khan supporters hold nationwide protests, demand political change
evidence.excerpt: After Imran Khan was shot, his supporters staged nationwide protests that sometimes clashed with security forces, and police used tear gas to disperse protesters blocking roads.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong independent contemporaneous coverage of a major domestic-security episode.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This shows the domestic unrest and force response during Sharif's tenure, but it does not establish a PM-specific order to use force.
contrary_evidence: The same report also says protesters blocked roads and some clashed with security forces, so the episode is not one-sided.

evidence.claim: The government began immediate cash distribution of Rs25,000 per affected family, and Sharif said relevant institutions were working daily with international partners to provide relief.
evidence.title: Govt starts immediate cash distribution among flood affectees in country: PM
evidence.excerpt: The government began immediate cash distribution of Rs25,000 per affected family, and Sharif said relevant institutions were working daily with international partners to provide relief.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official report with concrete cash-distribution details and direct PM remarks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct government response under Sharif, though still self-reported by state media.
contrary_evidence: The report reflects the start of disbursement, not full coverage or a final evaluation of adequacy.

evidence.claim: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif launched the Resilient Recovery Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Framework for the 2022 floods.
evidence.title: Govt launches '4R Framework' for Pakistan Floods 2022
evidence.excerpt: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif launched the Resilient Recovery Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Framework for the 2022 floods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official broadcaster report of a specific PM-launched recovery framework.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct PM-led recovery planning, though it remains a framework announcement rather than completed implementation.
contrary_evidence: A framework launch is not the same as measurable recovery success.

evidence.claim: Among the flood-affected were at least 650,000 pregnant women and girls, many of whom lacked access to the healthcare facilities and support needed for safe delivery.
evidence.title: Flood-Affected Women in Pakistan Need Urgent Help
evidence.excerpt: Among the flood-affected were at least 650,000 pregnant women and girls, many of whom lacked access to the healthcare facilities and support needed for safe delivery.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent rights analysis with concrete humanitarian figures and explicit protection concerns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is not Sharif-caused harm, but it is a direct test of the government's protection and relief response to a major domestic crisis.
contrary_evidence: The article focuses on urgent need, not on whether government relief ultimately reached everyone adequately.

evidence.claim: UN Women reported relief distributions, cash grants, women-friendly spaces, and gender-based-violence response services for flood-affected women and girls in Pakistan.
evidence.title: UN Women puts women and girls at the heart of flood response in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: UN Women reported relief distributions, cash grants, women-friendly spaces, and gender-based-violence response services for flood-affected women and girls in Pakistan.
evidence.source_locator: main article text on relief items and service scale-up
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN program update with concrete service and relief actions.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and directly relevant to flood response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is government-and-UN-coordinated crisis response under Sharif, though execution involved UN partners rather than the PM alone.
contrary_evidence: The page shows active response, but not whether all protection needs were met.
